title: Policy-Anchored Access Chronicle and Evidence Timeline
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This document defines a policy-anchored access chronicle: a structured, reproducible timeline and evidence packaging approach for all authorization-relevant events tied to policy changes, role updates, and access-exception decisions. The goal is to make compliance reviews (internal and external) fast and defensible by linking policy artifacts to a curated set of telemetry, decision records, and retention markers.

Scope

- Applies to all customer-facing and internal services that rely on Redwood RBAC and service-to-service authorization.
- Covers policy changes (authoring, approval, deployment), entitlement grants/denials, exception workflows, and retention handoff for audit evidence.
- Integrates with the audit logging, data residency, and secure SDLC controls described elsewhere.

Key definitions

- Policy snapshot: a versioned canonical copy of an access policy at a point in time (policy ID + git commit + checksum).
- Chronicle entry: a single row in the access timeline containing a pointer to the policy snapshot, the trigger event, and associated evidence bundle id.
- Evidence bundle: a packaged artifact (signed manifest) containing the minimum artifacts required for audit (logs, config diffs, approver attestations, deployment records).

Owner and responsibilities

- Security (owner): maintain chronicle templates, retention mappings, and signing keys for evidence bundles.
- Eng-Platform: ensure automated emission of chronicle entries to the evidence pipeline for policy deploys.
- Eng-SRE: provide durable storage and query access to audit logs referenced by bundles.
- Product / Legal: act as reviewers for high-risk policy exceptions and approve long-term retention.

Table: Evidence artifact minimal schema (for bundle manifest)

| field | description | example | retention | responsible |
|-------|-------------|---------|-----------|-------------|
| bundle_id | unique UUID for the evidence bundle | eb-3f9a8a | 7 years or as required by customer jurisdiction | Security |
| policy_id | canonical policy name + version | rbac/tenant-isolation@v3 | 7 years | Security |
| git_commit | commit hash for policy artifact in repo | a1b2c3d4 | 7 years | Eng-Platform |
| deploy_job | CI job id that deployed the policy | ci/deploy/4872 | 2 years | Eng-Platform |
| approvers | list of approver emails and timestamps | alice@redwood.com (2026-07-11T09:15Z) | 7 years | Product/Legal |
| evidence_refs | list of log query refs and storage URIs | s3://audit/2026/07/access.log#query-123 | see retention-mapping | Eng-SRE |

Policy change -> chronicle pipeline (high level)

1) Authoring: policy author opens a policy PR in the access-control repo. The PR must include a short rationale and test rules (unit tests that assert deny/allow for canonical identities).
2) Approval: two approvers required for medium/high-risk policies. Approvers add a signed attestation comment following the template.
3) Deployment: CI builds a policy snapshot, writes a snapshot artifact to artifacts.redwood.com, and emits a chronicle event to the Evidence Queue (kafka topic: evidence.chronicle).
4) Evidence bundling: a scheduled worker listens on evidence.chronicle, collects related logs, deployment metadata, and approver attestations, then creates a signed evidence bundle and stores it in the evidence archive.
5) Indexing: bundle metadata is indexed into the Evidence Index and a chronicle entry is appended to the running timeline for the policy_id.

Procedural checklist (operators)

- Before approving a policy PR: verify unit-tests and run the policy simulator against the weekly access-snapshot.
- On deployment: confirm the CI job produced a policy snapshot and that the policy checksum matches the artifact uploaded.
- If an approver uses delegated approval (JIT workflows): ensure the delegation token and minutes are captured in the approver record.

Automated evidence collection queries (examples)

- Authz decision trail (KQL):
  logs | where service == "authz" and policy_id == "rbac/tenant-isolation@v3" and timestamp between (start, end) | project timestamp, principal, resource, decision, reason

- Deployment metadata (SQL):
  SELECT job_id, commit, status, started_at, finished_at FROM ci_runs WHERE job_id = 'ci/deploy/4872';

- Bundle creation CLI (example):
  redwood evidence bundle create --policy rbac/tenant-isolation@v3 --commit a1b2c3d4 --ci-job ci/deploy/4872 --approvers alice@example.com,bob@example.com --output s3://evidence-archive/eb-3f9a8a.json

Retention mapping and cross-border considerations

- Default retention for evidence bundles: 7 years for enterprise customers in regulated sectors. Shorter retention (1–2 years) allowed for internal-only policies where no customer data is implicated, subject to Security review.
- Data residency: evidence bundles may contain log snippets that are subject to data residency rules. Sensitive logs (containing customer PII) must be redacted or stored in the customer-region evidence vault. See "Geo-fenced access forensics" for vault rules.

Exception handling and risk acceptance

- Temporary exceptions must use the Exception Request form (link in Related pages). Each exception creates a temporary policy wrapper and an exception bundle. Exception bundles must include: risk assessment, compensating controls, approved expiry, and monitoring hooks.
- Risk acceptance is recorded as part of the evidence bundle under approvers and a short reason string. Long-lived exceptions (>90 days) require an executive-level review and separate documentary evidence.

Audit and reviewer workflow (for compliance teams)

1) Query Evidence Index for policy_id and time window.
2) Retrieve associated evidence_bundle(s).
3) Verify bundle signature and manifest fields.
4) Execute provided log queries reproducibly using the stored query refs.
5) For any gaps, raise a Request-for-Information (RFI) ticket and attach it to the bundle. The RFI must be resolved and appended to the bundle before closing the audit window.

Operational runbook (incident tie-in)

- If an incident implicates authorization (e.g., unexpected cross-tenant access):
  1) Triage: mark incident as authz-sensitive and notify Security oncall.
  2) Snapshot: trigger an immediate evidence bundle for the implicated policy_id and time range (use CLI with --ad-hoc flag).
  3) Containment: apply temporary rollback to prior policy snapshot if authorized and record the rollback in a follow-up bundle.
  4) Post-incident review: attach postmortem to the chronicle entries and update the policy PR with corrective tests.

Quality gates and SDLC integration

- All policy artifacts must pass the Secure SDLC gates: unit tests, policy linting, and static analysis for wildcard rules.
- CI enforces that any PR that changes high-risk rules cannot be merged without a signed attestation from Product and Security. Merge is blocked otherwise.

Example: timeline for a policy amendment (illustrative)

- 2027-01-04 08:23Z: PR opened (author: devops-team). Rationale: restrict tenant cross-call.
- 2027-01-04 13:10Z: Automated policy simulator run: 12 failing test vectors flagged.
- 2027-01-05 09:00Z: Approver: Patricia Gomez (security) added signed attestation.
- 2027-01-05 09:24Z: CI deploy job ci/deploy/6123 succeeded, snapshot eb-7d2b4f created. Evidence bundle eb-7d2b4f stored in s3://evidence-archive/.
- 2027-01-05 09:30Z: Chronicle entry appended, evidence-index id idx-9852.

  "bundle_id": "eb-7d2b4f",
  "policy_id": "rbac/tenant-isolation@v4",
  "git_commit": "f7e3d2c1",
  "deploy_job": "ci/deploy/6123",
  "approvers": ["patricia@redwood.com (2027-01-05T09:00Z)"],
  "evidence_refs": ["s3://audit/2027/01/authz.log#query-6123"]
}
